trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the affordable ADO airport bus (approx. $10 USD) to the Hotel Zone. Check in to Cancun Beach Resort and get settled.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a short walk or local bus ride (Route 1 bus costs under $1 USD) to the nearest public beach stretch near the hotel. Relax, swim, and soak in your first views of the turquoise Caribbean waters. No entrance fee required for public beach access.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hotel Zone boulevard and grab dinner at one of the nearby local taco stands or casual restaurants. Explore the area around the hotel to get your bearings and enjoy the sunset over the lagoon side.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing — airport convenience store items or a small café bite to tide you over.
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable street tacos or a torta from a local food stand near the hotel zone for around $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Eat at La Parrilla or a similar casual Mexican restaurant in the Hotel Zone offering combo meals for $8–12 USD. Look for set menu specials (comida corrida).

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11 AM, allow 1.5–2 hours for immigration, baggage, and transit to the hotel. Don't overplan Day 1 — rest and orientation are key. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data access.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Playa Delfines for a full beach day experience. This iconic public beach is one of Cancun's most beautiful and least commercialized stretches, with stunning views of the Hotel Zone sign. Arrive early (around 9 AM) to claim a good spot. Entry is completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Playa Delfines — swim in the waves, build sandcastles, or simply relax under the sun. Walk along the shoreline and take photos of the famous 'Cancun' sign landmark. Vendors nearby sell cold drinks and snacks at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Take the local Route 1 bus back toward the hotel zone and explore Mercado 28, a local market where you can browse souvenirs and enjoy authentic, budget-friendly Mexican cuisine at the market's food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel if breakfast is included, or stop at a OXXO convenience store for yogurt, fruit, and a coffee for under $4 USD.
meals.lunch: Buy snacks and drinks from beach vendors or bring a packed lunch — grab items from a local grocery store (Chedraui or Walmart) the night before for $3–5 USD total.
meals.dinner: Dine at the food stalls inside Mercado 28. Try cochinita pibil tacos, sopa de lima, or enchiladas for $5–8 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with free parking and restroom facilities. The Route 1 bus runs the entire Hotel Zone and costs less than $1 USD per ride — it's the best budget transport option. Bring sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and cash for vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Akumal Bay for sea turtle snorkeling. Depart early by catching the ADO bus from Cancun to Akumal (approx. $10–12 USD each way, about 1.5 hours). Arrive at Akumal Bay and rent snorkel gear from a local shop on the beach for around $10–15 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon snorkeling in the calm, shallow waters of Akumal Bay where wild sea turtles graze on seagrass. No guided tour is required — you can snorkel independently from the public beach area. Explore the bay, spot sea turtles up close, and enjoy the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Cancun via ADO bus. Arrive back at the hotel by early evening. Relax and freshen up before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat a hearty breakfast before departure — try a local comedor near the hotel for eggs, beans, tortillas, and coffee for $4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: Grab lunch in Akumal village at one of the small beach restaurants or taco shops. Fish tacos and ceviche tostadas run $6–10 USD.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from a local supermarket (Chedraui nearby), or grab affordable street food near the hotel for $4–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book the ADO bus tickets in advance online or at the terminal to secure your seat. Akumal's public beach area is free to access — avoid paying for expensive guided tours as independent snorkeling is equally rewarding. Bring an underwater camera or waterproof phone case. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only, as chemical sunscreens are restricted in protected marine areas.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local neighborhood of Downtown Cancun (El Centro) by taking the cheap city bus. Visit Parque Las Palapas, a charming central plaza with local vendors, street performers, and authentic Mexican atmosphere. Browse the area and enjoy the local culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Playa Tortuga or Playa Caracol, two more free public beaches in the Hotel Zone with calmer waters ideal for swimming. Spend a relaxed afternoon beach-hopping and enjoying the Caribbean Sea. Both beaches are easily accessible by the Route 1 bus.
day_by_day.evening: Return to El Centro for the evening. Explore the lively Parque Las Palapas night market scene where local artisans sell crafts and food vendors offer cheap, delicious snacks.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local panadería (bakery) in El Centro for fresh pan dulce and café de olla for under $3 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local comedor in El Centro — a full set lunch menu (comida corrida) with soup, main dish, and drink costs $5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Enjoy street food at Parque Las Palapas — try marquesitas (crispy crepes with fillings), elotes, and aguas frescas for $3–5 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: El Centro is where locals live and eat — prices here are significantly lower than in the Hotel Zone. The city bus from the Hotel Zone to El Centro costs under $1 USD. Parque Las Palapas comes alive in the evenings with families and street vendors — a wonderful authentic Mexican experience.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at a quieter section of the Hotel Zone beach near the hotel. Enjoy a slow morning swim, read a book, and relax. Alternatively, rent a kayak or paddleboard from a budget beach rental shop for $10–15 USD per hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Museo Maya de Cancun (small entrance fee of approx. $4 USD) and the adjacent San Miguelito archaeological site to explore ancient Mayan ruins right in the Hotel Zone. This is a hidden gem that most budget travelers overlook.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Hotel Zone's main boulevard (Blvd. Kukulcan) at sunset for beautiful lagoon and sea views. Find a happy hour deal at a local bar or grab drinks from a convenience store and enjoy the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Make a simple breakfast with groceries from the supermarket — yogurt, fruit, granola, and juice for under $4 USD.
meals.lunch: Try La Fisheria or a similar casual seafood spot offering affordable lunch specials. Alternatively, grab a cemita or torta from a street vendor for $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Visit one of the taco restaurants in the Hotel Zone that offer budget-friendly combo deals — aim for $8–12 USD. Look for 2-for-1 taco specials common on weekday evenings.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Maya de Cancun is one of the best-value cultural experiences in the city and often overlooked by tourists. Sunday admission is free for Mexican nationals but foreigners pay a small fee on all days. The kayak and paddleboard rentals are best negotiated directly on the beach — avoid hotel desks which charge premium prices.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy one final morning at the beach near the hotel. Take a last swim in the Caribbean Sea and soak up the sun. Pack up your belongings and check out of the hotel (store luggage at the front desk if your flight is later in the day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon doing some budget souvenir shopping at Mercado 28 or Ki Huic market in El Centro, where prices are much lower than Hotel Zone shops. Pick up handmade crafts, vanilla extract, spices, and other Mexican souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport via ADO bus (approx. $10 USD) with enough time before your departure flight. Enjoy one last Mexican snack or meal before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Have a final Mexican breakfast at a local comedor — huevos rancheros or chilaquiles with coffee for $5–7 USD.
meals.lunch: Grab a final round of street tacos or a torta near Mercado 28 for $4–6 USD — a delicious and affordable last meal in Cancun.
meals.dinner: Eat at the airport if your flight departs in the evening, or have a light snack from a convenience store to keep costs low — budget $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the ADO bus ride and airport check-in/security. The ADO bus to the airport departs regularly from stops throughout the Hotel Zone. Confirm your hotel's luggage storage policy at check-out to keep your hands free for last-minute exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the resort beach or nearby Hotel Zone beach stretch for a relaxing first afternoon. Take a leisurely stroll along the Cancun Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) boulevard to get your bearings, browse local shops, and soak in the Caribbean atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the Hotel Zone. Explore the lively Punta Cancun area and take an evening walk along the lagoon-side promenade to wind down after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a light snack upon arrival at the resort
meals.lunch: La Habichuela Downtown or a casual beachside palapa restaurant near the Hotel Zone — try fish tacos and fresh ceviche (~$10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: La Parrilla Cancun — a popular mid-range Mexican grill with live mariachi music, great for a festive first night (~$20–30 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight arrives at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 light and relaxed. Early check-in may not be guaranteed — confirm with the resort in advance or store luggage with the concierge if the room isn't ready. Exchange some currency or locate a nearby ATM for cash tips and local purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort, then head to Playa Delfines Beach Day — one of Cancun's most beautiful and uncrowded public beaches. Arrive early to claim a good spot, swim in the turquoise Caribbean waters, and admire the iconic 'Cancun' sign for photos. The beach is free and offers stunning views of the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Playa Delfines or rent a beach chair and umbrella. Explore the natural dunes and enjoy the calmer, less commercialized atmosphere compared to hotel beaches. Take a short taxi or bus ride back toward the Hotel Zone and visit Mercado 28 for souvenir shopping and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up, then head out for dinner and a casual evening in the Hotel Zone. Enjoy the vibrant nightlife ambiance along Boulevard Kukulcan.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a nearby café — fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and coffee (~$10–15 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and drinks from a local convenience store (OXXO) for the beach, or grab fresh seafood at a casual beachside stand near Playa Delfines (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Labna Restaurant — authentic Yucatecan cuisine with dishes like cochinita pibil and sopa de lima in a charming mid-range setting (~$18–25 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is accessible via the Ruta 1 public bus along Boulevard Kukulcan — a very affordable option (~$0.80 USD). Apply plenty of reef-safe sunscreen and bring plenty of water. Waves can be stronger here than at hotel beaches, so swim with caution.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: Isla Mujeres Snorkeling and Beach Tour. Take an early ferry from Puerto Juarez or Playa Tortugas (departures from ~8:00–9:00 AM) to the charming island of Isla Mujeres. Explore the colorful streets of the island village by golf cart rental, visit the Punta Sur cliff viewpoint, and discover the local charm of this Caribbean gem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided snorkeling tour from Isla Mujeres to explore the crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and vibrant coral reefs. Relax on Playa Norte — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico — with its calm, shallow turquoise waters and white sand. Rent a beach lounger and enjoy the laid-back island vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Take the late afternoon ferry back to Cancun (last ferries around 6:00–7:00 PM). Return to the resort, freshen up, and enjoy a relaxed dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort or a grab-and-go option before the ferry — fruit, yogurt, or a pastry
meals.lunch: Lunch on Isla Mujeres at Playa Norte — try fresh grilled fish, shrimp tacos, or ceviche at a beachside restaurant like El Patio or Mango Cafe (~$12–18 USD)
meals.dinner: Sunset Grill or a Hotel Zone seafood restaurant back in Cancun — grilled lobster, shrimp fajitas, or fish of the day (~$20–28 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Isla Mujeres snorkeling tour in advance through the resort concierge or a reputable local operator. Round-trip ferry tickets cost approximately $8–12 USD. Golf cart rental on the island runs about $40–60 USD for a few hours and is the most fun way to explore. Bring cash, reef-safe sunscreen, a light cover-up, and a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Akumal Bay Sea Turtle Snorkeling. Depart early by rental car or organized tour (~1.5 hours south of Cancun along Highway 307). Arrive at Akumal Bay and snorkel in the calm, shallow waters where wild sea turtles graze on seagrass just meters from shore. This is a magical, bucket-list wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling with the turtles, explore the nearby town of Akumal, relax on the beach, or visit the Half Moon Bay area for more snorkeling. On the drive back, stop at a roadside taqueria or local restaurant for an authentic Yucatecan lunch experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun in the late afternoon. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a memorable evening sunset catamaran cruise — sail along the Caribbean coastline as the sun sets over the lagoon with open bar, snacks, and music.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, toast, fresh juice to fuel the day
meals.lunch: Roadside taqueria or casual local restaurant near Akumal or Tulum — cochinita pibil tacos, agua fresca, and fresh guacamole (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Light bites and drinks are typically included on the Sunset Catamaran Cruise. If still hungry afterward, grab a casual bite at a Hotel Zone restaurant or resort bar (~$10–15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Akumal snorkeling trip and Sunset Catamaran Cruise in advance — both are popular and fill up quickly. At Akumal, hire a certified local guide (~$15–20 USD) to help locate turtles and ensure responsible wildlife interaction. Do not touch or chase the turtles. The catamaran cruise typically departs around 5:00–6:00 PM and lasts 2–2.5 hours — confirm timing with the operator.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day adventure at Xel-Ha Eco Water Park and Snorkeling. Depart after breakfast for this natural aquatic theme park (~1.5 hours south). Snorkel through mangrove channels and the stunning coastal lagoon teeming with tropical fish. The all-inclusive entrance fee covers food, drinks, snorkeling gear, life jackets, and most activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Ha — try cliff jumping at the lookout point, float down the lazy river channel, ride bikes along the jungle trail, or relax in the natural pools. Take advantage of the included buffet lunch and refreshing drinks at the park's restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun in the late afternoon. Spend a final relaxed evening at the resort — enjoy the pool, a spa treatment if desired, or a sunset cocktail at the resort bar. Treat yourself to a special farewell dinner at one of the Hotel Zone's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — make it hearty since Xel-Ha is a full active day
meals.lunch: Included in the Xel-Ha all-inclusive entrance — enjoy the buffet with fresh seafood, Mexican dishes, salads, and tropical drinks
meals.dinner: Harry's Cancun — an upscale-casual steakhouse and seafood restaurant on the lagoon with a beautiful waterfront setting, perfect for a special farewell dinner (~$30–45 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Xel-Ha tickets in advance online for a discount (all-inclusive packages run ~$80–110 USD per person). Arrive early to maximize your time — the park opens at 8:30 AM. Wear your swimsuit under clothes, bring reef-safe sunscreen (required at the park), and a waterproof camera or GoPro. The park provides lockers, towels, and snorkeling equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Take one final walk or swim at the resort beach, soaking in the Caribbean views. Pack up and check out of the resort (standard checkout is typically 11:00 AM — request late checkout if your flight allows).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, spend any remaining hours exploring the Hotel Zone, picking up last-minute souvenirs at Mercado 28 or La Isla Shopping Mall, or relaxing at a nearby café. Arrange airport transfer to Cancun International Airport with plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cancun with wonderful beach memories, a sun-kissed glow, and a camera full of incredible Caribbean moments.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or a café treat — enjoy fresh tropical fruit, chilaquiles, or huevos rancheros one last time (~$10–15 USD)
meals.lunch: Quick, casual lunch near the Hotel Zone or airport area — fish tacos, a torta, or a fresh smoothie bowl (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure schedule

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for Cancun Airport check-in, security, and customs. Keep some Mexican pesos for tips and any last-minute purchases. Confirm your resort's checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a few extra hours. Don't forget to declare any goods purchased over the duty-free allowance.

Enjoy a welcome amenity and familiarize yourself with the resort's world-class facilities including pools, spa menu, and beach access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Playa Delfines Beach Day — Head to one of Cancun's most scenic and uncrowded public beaches just a short distance along the Hotel Zone. Relax on the powdery white sand, take a dip in the turquoise Caribbean waters, and soak in panoramic views of the coastline. Return to the resort mid-afternoon to freshen up and enjoy the resort pool or spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's rooftop or beachfront bar, watching the Caribbean sky turn golden. Dress up for a refined dinner experience to kick off the trip in style.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: La Habichuela Downtown — A Cancun institution known for its creative Yucatecan and Caribbean cuisine in a lush garden setting. Perfect for a celebratory first lunch.
meals.dinner: Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar — One of Cancun's most prestigious dining establishments on the lagoon, offering premium cuts, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine cellar with stunning waterfront views.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible given the 11:00 AM arrival. Keep Day 1 light to allow time to acclimate, hydrate, and recover from travel. Apply high-SPF sunscreen before any beach exposure.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a full morning of relaxation at the resort's private beach. Arrange for a premium beach cabana setup with chilled towels, fruit platters, and butler service. Take a morning swim in the calm Caribbean waters and enjoy the serenity before the day begins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sunset Catamaran Cruise preparation — Before the evening cruise, spend the afternoon at the resort's luxury spa. Indulge in a signature couples or solo treatment such as a Mayan-inspired body wrap or deep tissue massage. Afterward, enjoy the infinity pool with lagoon views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Cruise — Board a premium catamaran along the Caribbean coastline as the sun dips below the lagoon horizon. Enjoy an open bar with top-shelf cocktails, fresh snacks, and live music. The golden hour views from the water are absolutely breathtaking and quintessentially Cancun.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast at the main restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, eggs benedict, freshly squeezed juices, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Lorenzillo's — An iconic Cancun seafood restaurant built over the lagoon, offering fresh lobster, ceviche, and grilled fish in an elegant open-air setting.
meals.dinner: Light post-cruise dinner at the resort's beach grill — fresh grilled seafood, guacamole, and chilled white wine under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sunset Catamaran Cruise in advance to secure premium seating. Bring a light wrap or layer as it can get breezy on the water after sunset. Confirm whether the catamaran offers private or semi-private options for a more exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Isla Mujeres Snorkeling and Beach Tour — Depart early via private ferry or luxury water taxi to the charming island of Isla Mujeres. Explore the crystal-clear waters teeming with vibrant marine life including colorful reef fish, rays, and coral formations. A professional guide will lead the snorkeling excursion to the best spots around the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Isla Mujeres — Stroll through the colorful, pedestrian-friendly streets of the island village. Visit Punta Sur, the easternmost point of Mexico, for dramatic cliff views and the Mayan ruins of Ixchel. Rent a golf cart to tour the island at your own pace and discover hidden beach coves.
day_by_day.evening: Return via private water taxi to Cancun in time for a luxurious dinner. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Mango Café on Isla Mujeres — A beloved island gem offering fresh seafood, tropical salads, and the famous lobster pizza in a breezy beachside setting.
meals.dinner: Porfirio's Cancun — A sophisticated Mexican restaurant in the Hotel Zone featuring elevated traditional Mexican cuisine, premium tequila selections, and a vibrant yet refined atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for the ferry by 8:30–9:00 AM to maximize island time. Bring waterproof sunscreen, reef-safe preferred. Isla Mujeres is best explored by golf cart — pre-book or rent upon arrival. Carry cash in Mexican pesos for local vendors on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Akumal Bay Sea Turtle Snorkeling — Take a private luxury transfer south along the Riviera Maya to Akumal Bay, approximately 90 minutes from Cancun. Snorkel in the calm, shallow turquoise bay where wild green sea turtles graze peacefully on seagrass just meters from shore. This is one of the most magical wildlife encounters in the Caribbean.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Akumal, continue to the nearby town of Tulum for an afternoon of exploration. Visit the dramatic clifftop Mayan ruins of Tulum overlooking the Caribbean Sea — a breathtaking combination of ancient history and natural beauty. Afterward, relax on the pristine beach below the ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun via private transfer. Enjoy a serene evening at the resort — perhaps a nightcap at the bar or a moonlit walk along the beach.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure — huevos rancheros, fresh-baked pastries, tropical fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Hartwood in Tulum — One of the most celebrated restaurants on the Riviera Maya, using wood-fire cooking and locally sourced ingredients. Reservations are essential and highly recommended.
meals.dinner: In-resort fine dining — Request the resort's chef's tasting menu or a private beach dinner setup for a romantic and exclusive experience under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Book a private guided snorkeling tour at Akumal for the best sea turtle encounter experience and to avoid crowds. Tulum ruins open at 8:00 AM — visiting in the afternoon means more visitors, so plan accordingly. Pre-book Hartwood well in advance as it fills up weeks ahead. Confirm private transfer for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Xel-Ha Eco Water Park and Snorkeling — Journey to the stunning natural aquatic park of Xel-Ha, built around a breathtaking coastal lagoon. Snorkel through mangroves and cenote-fed waters teeming with tropical fish, float down lazy rivers, and explore the lush jungle surroundings. Opt for the all-inclusive VIP package for premium amenities and skip-the-line access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Xel-Ha's extensive offerings — cliff jumping platforms, hammocks over the water, paddleboarding, and zip lines over the lagoon. Take time to relax in the natural pools and enjoy the all-inclusive food and beverage offerings included in the VIP package.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun and transition into a festive final full-evening celebration. Explore the Cancun Hotel Zone nightlife or enjoy a premium dining experience to commemorate the penultimate night of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure.
meals.lunch: All-inclusive dining at Xel-Ha — Fresh seafood, grilled meats, tropical fruits, and unlimited beverages are included in the VIP package. Enjoy a leisurely lunch with your feet in the water.
meals.dinner: La Destilería — A premium Mexican restaurant and tequila museum in the Hotel Zone, offering an extensive tequila collection, exceptional Oaxacan cuisine, and a festive yet upscale ambiance perfect for a celebratory final evening dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the All-Inclusive Plus or VIP package at Xel-Ha for the best experience — it includes equipment rental, lockers, towels, and food and beverages. Bring reef-safe sunscreen as chemical sunscreens are prohibited to protect the ecosystem. The park opens at 9:00 AM — arrive early to enjoy it before crowds build up. Wear water shoes for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the resort's private beach. Enjoy a slow, indulgent farewell breakfast at the resort. Take a final dip in the Caribbean Sea or the pool. Pack up, check out, and arrange a private luxury transfer to Cancun International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight departure time, use any remaining time to browse duty-free shops at the airport for premium Mexican souvenirs — artisan goods, high-quality tequila, Oaxacan chocolate, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cancun with unforgettable memories of pristine beaches, vibrant marine life, ancient ruins, and world-class cuisine. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — a full spread of Mexican and continental favorites, fresh juices, and specialty coffee to savor the last morning in paradise.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or an early lunch at the resort before checkout — ceviche, tacos, and a fresh agua fresca.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort — request a late checkout if your flight departs in the afternoon or evening. Pre-arrange private airport transfer to ensure a seamless and stress-free departure. Arrive at Cancun International Airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international flight departure. Declare any food or agricultural items at customs upon return.
